To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in a sample of Urban Hispanics the prevalence of MS is greater in individuals with GAs than in normal fasting glucose individuals and that subjects with combined GA and DM had the highest prevalence of MS and the greatest number of traits per subject.
the association of GAs with the early appearance and the severity of traits of MS is strong and independent of the type of GA.

1) the association between the early appearance of MS traits and GAs is stronger than that previously reported; 2) GAs are associated with the presence of more MS traits, and each of the coexistent MS traits is more severe than in normal fasting glucose individuals; and 3) subjects with newly diagnosed type 1 DM and with combined GA (IFG +IGT) have a greater number of MS traits, and more severe MS traits than subjects with isolated IFGs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association of GAs with the early appearance and severity of MS.
the early detection of GAs, and the early identification of the MS.
the early identification of subjects who will develop type 2 DM and/or cardiovascular disease, and with their early treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
subjects with combined IFG +IGT and newly diagnosed type II diabetes have the greatest prevalence of MS and the greatest severity of each trait of the MS.
the MS is an early and integral component of the natural history of GAs.
the MS is a common finding in all types of GAs and that it is more severe in the presence of multiple GA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of GAs is associated with an increased number of traits of MS and that the severity of each of these traits is greater in individuals with GAs.
the MS is the common pathway for the early development of type 2 DM.

the presence of GA is a strong predictor of the early onset of the MS, and that the severity of GA is directly associated with the number of traits of MS and with the severity of each of its coexisting traits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of the metabolic syndrome is associated with an increased prevalence of glucose abnormalities.
the presence of any GA in an individual is a warning signal for the presence of the MS and its associated metabolic and cardiovascular risk.

in subjects with combined IFG +IGT, the MS was characterized not only by the presence of multiple traits, but also by their greater severity, as compared with subjects with isolated IFGs and isolated IGTs.
